findings.issue: Creator.affiliations has declared range Organization[] and each entry carries `name`, but only the top-level Creator slot inventory names `affiliations`; the individual affiliation objects list only Massachusetts General Hospital, University of Florida, UTHealth Houston and Tufts University, while the bundle states the collaboration spans 20 academic centers of which 14 are Data Acquisition centers. The four listed are the institutions of the named leadership team, not the creator organization set. Supported, but the object as written conflates leadership affiliation with consortium composition; the qualifier lives only in `notes`.

Creator `name: CHoRUS Consortium` is paired with `principal_investigator: Rosenthal, Eric S.` The bundle supports Rosenthal as PI of NIH project 10472824 (organization: Massachusetts General Hospital) but never designates him PI of the consortium as a creator entity. The composition is an inference joining two distinct source statements.

`counts: 50000` is asserted as the instance count while the same object's `notes` records a conflicting figure (over 45,000 unique admissions, August 2025) and an anticipated 100,000. The bundle gives no basis for privileging 50,000 as the instance count in a structured numeric slot; the conflict is disclosed only in prose. Same construction in the core record.

`counts: 7642` is placed on an object whose `instance_type` is 'Imaging study extracted from hospital PACS'. The bundle states '7,642 Admissions with Radiology Data' — a count of admissions, not of imaging studies. The number is attached to the wrong unit of instance.

B2AI_SUBSTRATE:37 (Relational Database) is assigned to OMOP rows. The bundle says the data are standardized to the OMOP Common Data Model and held in a cloud enclave; it never states a relational database substrate. The term is an approximation where the digest instructs omission.

'The released waveform data total 23 terabytes' is attached to the telemetry-waveform instance. The bundle's '23 Tb Waveform data' figure is undifferentiated across waveform modalities (telemetry and EEG); assigning it to telemetry alone narrows the source claim.

`anomalies: []` is an empty list. The bundle supports no anomaly statement either way; an explicit empty list asserts absence of known anomalies, which the bundle does not support. Omission is the correct treatment. (Core record correctly omits the slot.)

Includes `OTHER` without any indication of which standard it stands for. EDF+, Persyst and OHNLP are the unregistered standards named in `conforms_to`, but a single `OTHER` term cannot be resolved against three distinct standards, defeating the queryability the slot exists for.

`publisher: https://chorus4ai.org/` is identical to `id` and `page`. The bundle names no publisher entity for the dataset; the project website URL is being reused as a publisher identifier without support.

Free-text status is a synthesized characterization ('Under active acquisition and phased release'). The bundle's own status statement about the resource is the website banner 'This repoitory is under review for potential modification in compliance with Administration directives', which appears only in `notes`. The generated phrasing is an interpretation, not a source value.

Jared Houghtaling is placed in `committee_contact` (range Person). The bundle lists him only as one of two request-access email contacts on the GitHub README; no committee, committee membership, or contact role is described. The slot semantics (access committee contact) are not supported. The co-equal contact dbold@emory.edu is given no structured representation, so the choice between the two is arbitrary.

Conflates two distinct access paths without distinguishing them: general dataset access requests via two emails, and the AIM-AHEAD training-program registration/licensing/.edu-email route. The bundle presents the .edu requirement and registration form as program-specific; the composite prose implies a single review process.

`accountable_organization: CHoRUS Consortium` is asserted. The bundle names Massachusetts General Hospital as the NIH awardee organization and states the website content is 'solely the responsibility of the authors'; it never designates an accountable organization for the data. Inference.

`true` is derived from the presence of PICU and NICU admissions. The bundle states the cohort includes PICU and NICU admissions but never characterizes any population as at-risk or describes protections. The boolean converts a cohort-composition fact into a governance determination the sources do not make.

`was_directly_observed: true` is asserted for retrospective extraction of records generated during clinical care. The bundle describes retrospective data collection from hospital systems; whether this counts as direct observation is a schema-semantics judgment the sources do not license. The same object's prose ('rather than through a purpose-built collection from individuals', core record) sits in tension with the boolean.

The `direct_collection` object omits `is_direct` while its prose states data are obtained 'rather than through a purpose-built collection from individuals' — the boolean the slot exists to carry is left unpopulated and the determination is buried in text. Also an inconsistency with `acquisition_methods.was_directly_observed: true` in the same record.

Present in the full record (holdout test set) but absent from the core record, where the same holdout fact was folded into `sampling_strategies.strategies` prose. Paired records represent the same evidence in structurally divergent ways.

Slot omitted from the core record; the direct/indirect collection content was merged into `acquisition_methods.acquisition_details`. The core schema was not supplied in the digest, so the omission may be schema-driven, but it is an unreconciled structural divergence from the full record.
Omitted; holdout-set evidence relocated into `sampling_strategies`. Same divergence class as the full record's `splits`/`direct_collection` handling.

Omitted although the bundle supports enumerated terms: access requires a signed licensing agreement and an institutional (.edu) address, and the training-program route is program-scoped. Candidate values such as `institution_specific` or `project_specific` are available; the record leaves the queryable slot empty and states the terms only in prose.

Top-level `license` omitted. Defensible, since the MIT License in the bundle governs the GitHub software rather than the dataset and the record says so in `ip_restrictions` and `source_caveats`. Flagged only because the bundle does contain an explicit license string that a reader may expect to see reflected.

`role: other` is assigned to the GitHub-organization maintainer entry. The enum offers no fitting term for a code-hosting organization, but the entry itself is not a maintainer person or organization — it is a description of a repository space. The object populates a maintainer slot with infrastructure, not a maintaining party.

`role` carries multi-clause descriptive prose ('Data Acquisition centers: 14 of the 20 academic centers in the collaboration contribute clinical data extracts'), duplicating content that belongs in the sibling `collector_details`. DataCollector.role is untyped here, so this is not a validation failure, but the value is a description rather than a role designation. Same in the core record.

A `DatasetBias` object with `bias_type: representation_bias` is asserted, but its own `source_caveats` concedes the bundle reports only mitigation intent and design goals, never a measured or observed bias. A typed bias claim is being made where the evidence supports only a stated concern; the structured `bias_type` term outruns the source.

'CHoRUS consortium Ethics pillar (Ethical and Trustworthy AI)' is presented as a reviewing organization. The bundle describes Ethics as one of three project pillars conducting focus groups and legal analysis; it does not describe the pillar as conducting ethical review of the dataset. The mapping to EthicalReview overstates the pillar's function.

`involves_human_subjects: true` is asserted while `irb_approval`, `ethics_review_board` and `regulatory_compliance` are all left empty, with the gap explained in `notes`. Consistent with the bundle, but the record simultaneously populates `ethical_reviews` with a pillar-derived object, giving the misleading impression that ethical oversight is documented.

Omitted while `method` prose enumerates tokenization, local note retention and imaging de-identification. The bundle does not name specific identifier categories removed, so omission is correct; noted only for completeness of the de-identification object.

Each `format` value carries access-control and metadata-status commentary ('held in the cloud enclave under controlled access, with published metadata', 'Metadata publication planned') rather than a format designation alone. Access status and metadata availability are not format facts; the objects also leave `media_type`, `download_url` and `access_urls` empty.

`release_dates` contains narrative describing snapshots and the project end date rather than dates. The sibling `source_caveats` acknowledges no formal release dates exist, which argues for omitting the object rather than filling the slot with prose.

Both typed date slots are left empty while `timeframe_details` prose carries 2022-09-01 and 2026-11-30. Those dates are the funded project period, not the collection period, so populating the typed slots would be wrong — but the record then supplies no collection timeframe at all, and the object exists chiefly to restate project-period metadata already held in `funders.notes`.

Combines a supported dataset-use claim ('being used for training activities and publications') with extensive AIM-AHEAD program detail (up to 30 trainees, coursework, posters, manuscripts) that describes the training program rather than uses of the dataset. Program mechanics are being recorded as dataset use evidence.

Describes the AIM-AHEAD training curriculum (Jupyter notebooks, OHDSI tool stack, OMOP CDM instruction) as an intended use of the dataset. The bundle presents these as program training content; the dataset's role is as material used during training. The object attributes curriculum design to dataset intent.

The 'may support analyses of context and equity beyond bedside prediction tasks' claim is a generated extrapolation from the presence of SDoH and geocoding. The bundle names SDoH as an acquired data element but never suggests equity analysis as an additional supported task. Speculative.

Groups OHNLP toolkit, DeGauss, privacy_scan_tool and CTP-deid as annotation tools. Only OHNLP performs anything resembling annotation (extraction/tokenization); DeGauss is a geocoder and privacy_scan_tool/CTP-deid are de-identification utilities already recorded under `is_deidentified.method` and `preprocessing_strategies`. Three of four entries are misclassified and duplicated across slots.

`archival: false` is asserted for all four external resources. The bundle makes no statement about the archival status of the project website, GitHub organization, NIH RePORTER record, or webinar PDF. Four unsupported boolean assertions.

Describes contribution routes for data sites, clinical mappers and software developers to the CHoRUS project and its repositories. These are project contribution workflows, not mechanisms for extending or contributing to the dataset by external users; the bundle does not describe dataset extension by data recipients.

`frequency` omitted while `update_details` states sites 'provide regular status updates'. Correct omission (the bundle gives no interval), but note that the update_details content largely describes site status reporting to the project rather than a dataset update plan.

The single object cites CHoRUSReports characterization reports and SOP validation. The bundle describes CHoRUSReports as producing characterization reports returned to sites after submission — a feedback/QA artifact, not a documented cleaning procedure applied to the data. No outlier removal, deduplication or error correction is described anywhere in the bundle.

Includes 'equitable AI', which derives from the project title rather than describing dataset content, and 'intensive care unit', which restates 'critical care'. Minor: keyword list mixes project branding with content descriptors.

`subpopulation_elements_present: true` with an `identification` describing SDoH and geographic distance as acquired data elements. Data elements enabling subgroup characterization are not themselves a subpopulation; the object records variables in a slot reserved for represented groups. `variables` would be the fitting slot.

Omitted entirely, though the bundle enumerates concrete data elements in the webinar table (demographics, diagnoses, procedures, medication administration with dosing timestamps, nursing flowsheets, clinical notes, imaging, telemetry waveforms, EEG waveforms) plus geographic distance to nearest hospital. These are field-level descriptors the slot exists to hold; instead they are dispersed across `instances`, `description` and `subpopulations`.

Omitted while the bundle states 23 Tb of waveform data. Defensible, since 23 Tb covers waveforms only and not the whole dataset, and the units in the source ('Tb') are ambiguous — but the omission should be reflected in `source_caveats`, which mentions absence of byte size without noting the partial figure that does exist.

Carries the website compliance-review banner and the NIH disclaimer. The banner is a statement about the website/repository status and arguably belongs in `status`; the NIH disclaimer is boilerplate about the website rather than dataset content. Borderline use of the residual slot.

Records the program manager email as 'cmccrary@mgh.havard.edu' with an '(as printed)' annotation. Faithful transcription is correct, but embedding the source-fidelity annotation inside `notes` rather than `source_caveats` mixes trust commentary with content; the same annotation is duplicated in `maintainers.maintainer_details` and in top-level `source_caveats`.

`id` is the project website URL, which is also used for `page`, `publisher`, and as the base for every fragment identifier across the record. Functional, but the dataset is thereby identified with the project homepage; the bundle offers no dataset-specific identifier, DOI or accession, which `source_caveats` does acknowledge.

States the anticipated final dataset 'covers 100,000 patient admissions, nine data modalities, and 14 contributing hospitals' and the released set '50,000 patient admissions', then reports the August 2025 figure of over 45,000. Three mutually inconsistent scale figures are presented in a single narrative without indicating which describes the record's referent; `source_caveats` explains the conflict but the description reads as cumulative fact.

summary: Both records are broadly grounded in the declared bundle and disclose their principal source conflicts in `source_caveats`, but the audit finds a consistent pattern of structured slots outrunning the evidence they rest on. The most serious issues are: (1) typed assertions the bundle does not license — `data_governance.committee_contact` recasting an access-request email contact as a committee contact, `accountable_organization` naming an entity no source designates, `at_risk_populations.at_risk_groups_included: true` converting cohort composition into a governance determination, and `known_biases.bias_type: representation_bias` asserting a bias category where the bundle records only mitigation intent (the object's own source_caveats concedes this); (2) numeric misattribution — `instances[imaging].counts: 7642` attaches an admission count to an imaging-study instance, and `instances[admission].counts: 50000` privileges one of three conflicting scale figures in a structured slot while the conflict lives only in prose; (3) unsupported absence claims — `anomalies: []` in the full record asserts no known anomalies, and four `external_resources.archival: false` booleans assert archival status the bundle never addresses; (4) slot-semantics drift — `machine_annotation_tools` groups a geocoder and two de-identification utilities with the one genuine annotation tool and duplicates them across `preprocessing_strategies` and `is_deidentified`; `subpopulations[subpop-sdoh]` records data elements as a represented group; `extension_mechanism` describes project contribution workflows rather than dataset extension; `cleaning_strategies` cites a site-feedback artifact as a cleaning procedure. Clear supported omissions: `variables` is empty despite the webinar table enumerating nine data types with formats, access controls and metadata status — the single richest field-level source in the bundle — and `license_and_use_terms.data_use_permission` is unpopulated despite enumerable evidence (signed agreement, .edu institutional requirement, program-scoped access). Internal inconsistencies: the full record sets `acquisition_methods.was_directly_observed: true` while its `direct_collection` prose states collection was not from individuals, and leaves `direct_collection.is_direct` empty; the paired records diverge structurally, with `splits` and `direct_collection` present in the full record but dissolved into `sampling_strategies` and `acquisition_methods` prose in the core. Shape conformance is otherwise sound — no enum violations, no wrong-range values, no source commentary embedded in name or identifier fields (the '(as printed)' email annotations sit in `notes`, not in the values themselves), though `distribution_formats.format` and `distribution_dates.release_dates` carry access-status and narrative content rather than the format and date values their slots name. `conforms_to_standard` includes a bare `OTHER` standing for three distinct unregistered standards (EDF+, Persyst, OHNLP), which defeats the term's queryability.
